mutant.description: Mutants were planted ONLY where a scratch root is a faithful stand-in, and observed negatives used where it is not -- stated because a mutant that fails for the wrong reason is worse than none. PLANTED, in a root outside every worktree holding copies of the after-reads, the source map, the check and the self-contained .tools/aws shim, with the BASELINE run there first and reading PASS: (1) fresh_request.refused true -> false; (2) fresh_request.vendor_reached false -> true; (3) ledger.state CLOSED -> OPEN. All three target AC1, whose file inputs a copy reproduces exactly. NOT PLANTED, with reasons: AC3 runs git diff and git show IN the root, so a non-repository scratch copy would fail rc!=0 and FAIL for the wrong reason, proving nothing about discrimination; AC2's only inputs are the live role, with no file a copy could corrupt.

(3) FAIL: ledger {'state': 'OPEN'} | IB122-1-AC1 FAIL rc=1. Each was reverted and the baseline re-read PASS. OBSERVED NEGATIVES, which are the real world rather than a copy of it and are therefore stronger: for AC2, the role held 9 inline policies with BOTH session policies present, measured by this seat at the start of this act -- the exact state AC2 fails on; for AC3, the tree carried the release and the source-map entry was the release entry, measured by this seat as an 11-path delta against fb3bae3b99 before the restore, and independently by the issuer whose preflight records 'AC3 FAIL (tree carries the release)'. declared_exclusions.item: The retained vendor reports and the PERFORMANCE_USE# use records written while the release was live
declared_exclusions.reason: The order's bound forbids deleting or altering them: they are the record of what was served. They were left untouched. The use record COUNT is reported as 'not read' rather than zero, because the record is a DynamoDB PutItem that a log-group read does not reach.

declared_exclusions.item: Any vendor call to Black Diamond or Orion, and any secretsmanager get-secret-value
declared_exclusions.reason: Forbidden by the order's BOUNDS. None was made at any point in this act. The two secret data sources included in the destroy plan resolve a name to an ARN and never a value, and with count restored to 0 they are removed from state rather than read.

declared_exclusions.item: Driving a caller the function ADMITS for the fresh-request check
declared_exclusions.reason: This seat cannot supply a verified internal subject, which is why the order offers a second option and why IB-pr-423's live-call arm could not have caught the defect being rolled back. Option two was taken and recorded as such: the identical IB-pr-423 event plus the prescribed log read.

declared_exclusions.item: Any judgement on whether the IB-pr-423 release should have been ordered
declared_exclusions.reason: Not this seat's. The issuer states the apply was correct to its order and the order was wrong; the CTO ruled the rollback. This act executes the signed Branch B and records what moved.
